info.title: A.U.G.U.R Foresight — agent tool exchange
info.x-guidance: Call any tool with POST https://augur-trade.com/hub/api/v1/tools/{id} and a JSON body matching its schema. Paid tools answer HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements (Solana: USDC TransferChecked or native SOL to the payTo address; the exchange is its own facilitator and pays the network fee). Sign the transfer, retry with X-PAYMENT (v1) or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2) and you get the result plus a settlement receipt; you are only charged if the tool answered. Alternatives: a prepaid credit key (Authorization: Bearer hk_…) or X-PAYMENT-TX with a signature you already sent. Free tools need no payment; 10 free paid calls/day with header X-Synapse-Free: 1. Everything is read-only; pump.fun data is our own recording of every curve trade since 2026-09-11, other data comes from the providers listed in llms.txt, cached and paced so callers never see their rate limits.
info.description: A tool exchange for AI agents, run by an AI (A.L.F). 79 read-only tools: crypto markets and DeFi on every chain (prices, TVL, yields, stablecoins, perps funding, order books, gas, EVM contracts and token security), Solana and pump.fun intelligence from our own live recording of every bonding-curve trade, launch bundle forensics on Solana and 18 EVM chains (who bundled it, insiders, airdrops, serial devs), Meteora DLMM liquidity, reading and inspecting the web (clean page text, PDFs, DNS, WHOIS, TLS, robots), research (Wikipedia, arXiv, packages and CVEs, GitHub, Hacker News, DOIs, books), the physical world (weather, geocoding, FX, holidays, time zones, countries, earthquakes, sun/moon) and exact local utilities (QR, hashing, JSON Schema, cron, diff, units, JWT). MCP + HTTP. Pay per call via x402 in USDC or SOL on Solana or USDC on Base, or with prepaid credits. 10 free paid-tool calls per day; free tools are always free.

post.description: Live pump.fun heartbeat: trades/min, launches, graduations, graduation rate, hottest tokens in the last 15 min. Computed from our own live recording of every pump.fun bonding-curve trade. Use it to decide whether the launch market is hot or dead before scanning individual tokens.

pump.fun over time: launches, graduations, graduation rate, trades, SOL volume and unique wallets per day or hour since 2026-09-11 — with a compare window. The same tape as pump_pulse, sliced into UTC days or hours so an agent can compare the market over time instead of reading one snapshot. Pass compare_from/compare_to to get a second window and the per-period change (e.g. this week vs last week). Closed periods are precomputed from our own live recording of every bonding-curve trade; the open period is marked partial. Also reports the share of trades made by pump.fun's own mayhem agent, so it can be separated from real demand.

from.description: UTC start, e.g. 2026-09-18 or 2026-09-18T06 (default: 14 days / 48 hours back)

compare_from.description: start of a second window to compare against

compare_to.description: end of the comparison window, inclusive

post.description: Would copying this wallet have made money? Replays its pump.fun entries and exits 0–25 slots late on the recorded curve and shows where the edge dies. Takes the wallet's pump.fun positions over the last 1–14 days and simulates a copier that buys the same token and sells when the leader sells, arriving 0, 1, 2, 5, 10 or 25 slots (0–10 s) late. Fills use the bonding-curve reserves our tape recorded at that moment, including curve fees and the copy's own price impact. Returns PnL, win rate and ROI per latency, the leader's own median ROI for contrast, and a verdict: copyable, latency-sensitive (edge gone by N slots), or not copyable. A wallet that looks great on its own PnL often loses money for anyone who follows it.

Is this a valid address, and for which chain? EVM (with checksum fix), Solana (on-curve wallet vs PDA), Bitcoin (legacy/P2SH/SegWit/Taproot), Tron, Cosmos-style bech32. Pure checksum and format validation, no network calls. Catches the typo that would send funds to nowhere, and tells a Solana wallet (on curve) from a program-derived address.

post.description: Any public URL → clean readable markdown: the article/main content without nav, ads or boilerplate, plus title, author, date, word count and links. PDFs too. Fetches the page (redirects followed, public internet only), extracts the main content with Mozilla Readability and converts it to markdown. PDFs are converted to text. Use max_chars to bound the output. JavaScript-only pages return whatever the server sends (no headless browser).

Use to build link previews, check SEO/social cards, find a site's feeds or structured data. Flags missing og:image, missing description and non-absolute image URLs (common reasons a link shows up bare on X/Telegram).

post.description: All DNS for a domain — A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA, SOA — plus SPF and DMARC parsed and graded, so an agent knows where a domain points and whether its email can be spoofed. Queried live against public resolvers (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9). Email grade: SPF present and ending in -all/~all, DMARC present with p=quarantine/reject.

Who registered a domain and when: registrar, creation/expiry dates, age, days to expiry, status locks, nameservers — or that it looks available to register. Uses RDAP, the registries' official successor to WHOIS (rdap.org bootstrap). A domain with no RDAP record and no DNS is reported as likely available. Young domains (< 30 days) are flagged: most phishing/scam sites are days old.

post.description: Who bundled a Solana pump.fun launch: every block-0 wallet labelled sniper bot / bundle / dev-linked, supply bought and still held, holders who got tokens by transfer, serial-dev check, top-10 concentration, RugCheck — plus a back-tested skip/pass verdict. The rug guard A.U.G.U.R snipers use before every buy. Skip rules were tested on 2,221 real caller calls (held-out: stop-outs 10%→5%, rugs 16%→11%): creator launched another coin in the prior 24 h; top-10 wallets >35%; block-0 wallets that also bundled this creator's earlier launches; block-0 buys >20% of supply. Extra flags: RugCheck danger risks, insider wallets >15%, and >10% held by wallets that never bought on the curve (tokens moved in by transfer, the layered-bundle pattern of launch tools like Proxima). "ok:true" means no red flags were found, not that the coin is safe.

post.description: Who bundled an EVM token launch (Base, BSC, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Robinhood and 13 more): creation-tx airdrops to fake holders, first-seconds buys, scripted fixed-cadence buying, fresh-wallet and transfer-only holders, dev holdings, exchange-labelled holders, GoPlus contract flags — plus a skip/pass verdict. Replays every ERC-20 Transfer of the token from its first mint on the public RPC, so for young tokens (Base ~4 days, BSC ~6 h of history in budget) holder balances, buys and wallet-to-wallet hand-offs are exact. Launchpads (Four.meme, Uniswap v4 PoolManager, v2/v3 pairs from Dexscreener) are detected; vault/locker contracts that never bought are kept out of the wallet rules, while contracts that DID buy (smart wallets, bundler contracts) count as wallets. Older tokens fall back to GoPlus holders with 527 exchange wallets named. Skip rules: GoPlus honeypot/tax>10%/owner powers; top-10 wallets >35%; first ~2 s of buys >20%; >10% held by wallets that never bought; creation tx airdropping ≥10 wallets or >10%; scripted buying (≥5 buys ≥1% at a regular cadence taking ≥15%); fresh wallets / buyer contracts >15%. Heuristic on EVM (mirrors the back-tested Solana guard); "pass" is not a safety promise.
